at.name: at
at.description:
`size` compares against the nearest ancestor with `container-type` set.
A named step resolves here to a literal length, since at-rule
conditions evaluate before custom properties resolve.
at.summary: `size` compares against the nearest ancestor with `container-type` set.

atMax.name: atMax
atMax.description:
The `max-width` counterpart to at: applies while the nearest
container's inline size is at most `size`. Shares at's
named-scale/literal-length resolution and named-container targeting.
atMax.summary: The `max-width` counterpart to at: applies while the nearest container's inline size is at most `size`.

atQuery.name: atQuery
atQuery.description:
The raw escape hatch for expressing a container condition directly —
querying `height`, `orientation`, a style feature, or combining several
with `and`/`or`. `query` is used verbatim as the full `@container` condition.
atQuery.summary: The raw escape hatch for expressing a container condition directly — querying `height`, `orientation`, a style feature, or combining several with `and`/`or`.

contrastLess.name: contrastLess
contrastLess.description:
Sugar over `media("(prefers-contrast: less)", input)`.

Browser support for this query lags behind `contrastMore`, so keep a base
declaration alongside it to cover browsers that ignore the query.

contrastMore.name: contrastMore
contrastMore.description:
Sugar over `media("(prefers-contrast: more)", input)`.

The theme layer already strengthens every tone's `border` here; reach for
this wrapper to strengthen other properties, like a muted foreground.

forcedColors.name: forcedColors
forcedColors.description:
Sugar over `media("(forced-colors: active)", input)`. Forced-colors mode
swaps colors for a system palette — use this to restore non-color cues like
borders, or keep an element's own colors via `forced-color-adjust`.

media.name: media
media.description:
The explicit escape hatch for a real viewport/feature media query, for a
rule that must read the viewport or a user preference. `u.at()` handles
container-based responsive layout.
media.summary: The explicit escape hatch for a real viewport/feature media query, for a rule that must read the viewport or a user preference.

motionReduce.name: motionReduce
motionReduce.description:
Sugar over `media("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)", input)`.

Prefer `u.motionSafe()` when there is a choice: declaring motion only
inside the positive query lets a missing wrapper fall back to no motion.

motionSafe.name: motionSafe
motionSafe.description:
Sugar over `media("(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)", input)`. Styles
apply only when the user has not asked for less motion, so a missing
wrapper safely defaults to no animation.

print.name: print
print.description:
Sugar over `media("print", input)`. `"print"` is a media type, so it's
passed without parentheses — used to hide interactive chrome, force a
light surface, and expand truncated content back to full height on paper.

scheme.name: scheme
scheme.description:
Applies the given utilities under both the forced `.dark`/`.light` class
and the system-preference `.system` class behind `prefers-color-scheme`,
so both stay in sync. Composed from `u.when()` and `u.media()`.
scheme.summary: Applies the given utilities under both the forced `.dark`/`.light` class and the system-preference `.system` class behind `prefers-color-scheme`, so both stay in sync.

startingStyle.name: startingStyle
startingStyle.description:
Wraps utilities in `@starting-style`, defining the values a transition
animates from — for entry fade/scale-ins on dialogs, tooltips, popovers,
and other elements starting `display: none` or in the top layer.
startingStyle.summary: Wraps utilities in `@starting-style`, defining the values a transition animates from — for entry fade/scale-ins on dialogs, tooltips, popovers, and other elements starting `display: none` or in the top layer.

supports.name: supports
supports.description:
A feature-query wrapper, applying the given utilities only when the
browser supports `query` — progressive enhancement for CSS features
without a reliable fallback path other than "don't apply this at all".
supports.summary: A feature-query wrapper, applying the given utilities only when the browser supports `query` — progressive enhancement for CSS features without a reliable fallback path other than "don't apply this at all".

transparencyReduce.name: transparencyReduce
transparencyReduce.description:
Sugar over `media("(prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce)", input)`.

Supplies an explicit solid fallback — an opaque background, a stronger
border — for a surface styled only inside the no-preference branch.

transparencySafe.name: transparencySafe
transparencySafe.description:
Sugar over `media("(prefers-reduced-transparency: no-preference)", input)`,
the same gate `u.translucent()` uses internally. Wrap `u.backdropBlur()`
or `u.backdropSaturate()` in it directly to keep both effects gated together.
transparencySafe.summary: Sugar over `media("(prefers-reduced-transparency: no-preference)", input)`, the same gate `u.translucent()` uses internally.

calc.name: calc
calc.description:
Wraps a CSS `calc()` expression: `calc({expression})`. Returns a plain
string, usable anywhere a utility accepts a raw CSS value, typically with
`u.var()` to combine a custom property with an arithmetic operation.

combine.name: combine
combine.description:
Flattens `input` and merges the flattened utilities' style trees into one
declaration set at the host's own level, so unrelated utilities compose as
a single mixin with each nested selector kept as a sibling.
combine.summary: Flattens `input` and merges the flattened utilities' style trees into one declaration set at the host's own level, so unrelated utilities compose as a single mixin with each nested selector kept as a sibling.

counterIncrement.name: counterIncrement
counterIncrement.description:
Applies `counter-increment` to the element's CSS counter, named by the
bare counter identifier `name`. `value` is the integer the counter is
incremented by; omit it to fall back to CSS's own default of `1`.
counterIncrement.summary: Applies `counter-increment` to the element's CSS counter, named by the bare counter identifier `name`.

counterReset.name: counterReset
counterReset.description:
Applies `counter-reset`, creating or resetting the element's CSS counter
named by the bare counter identifier `name`. `value` is the integer the
counter is set to; omit it to fall back to CSS's own default of `0`.
counterReset.summary: Applies `counter-reset`, creating or resetting the element's CSS counter named by the bare counter identifier `name`.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description:
Applies `cursor`. Accepts any CursorValue keyword — `"pointer"` for
an interactive control, `"not-allowed"` for a disabled one, `"default"` to
force the plain arrow — or an arbitrary string for a `url(...)` cursor.

env.name: env
env.description:
Resolves a CSS environment variable reference: `env({name})`, or
`env({name}, {fallback})` when a fallback is given. Returns a plain string,
usable anywhere a utility accepts a raw CSS value.
env.summary: Resolves a CSS environment variable reference: `env({name})`, or `env({name}, {fallback})` when a fallback is given.

if.name: if
if.description:
Conditionally returns `input`, or a falsy value when `condition` is falsy.
`mix` already accepts falsy values directly (`mix={[cond && u.bg()]}`), so
this serves call sites that prefer a utility-shaped conditional.
if.summary: Conditionally returns `input`, or a falsy value when `condition` is falsy.

listStyle.name: listStyle
listStyle.description:
Applies `list-style`. Defaults to `"none"`, the common case of a `<ul>` or
`<ol>` serving as a plain layout container.

pointerEvents.name: pointerEvents
pointerEvents.description:
Applies `pointer-events`. Defaults to `"none"`, the common case of an
overlay, icon, or decorative element that should let clicks and hovers pass
through to whatever's underneath it.

pseudoContent.name: pseudoContent
pseudoContent.description:
Applies the CSS `content` property, almost always on a `::before`/`::after`
pseudo-element. The `pseudo` prefix keeps the name distinct from
`@sdxc/u/layout`'s `content()`, which sets `align-content`.
pseudoContent.summary: Applies the CSS `content` property, almost always on a `::before`/`::after` pseudo-element.

raw.name: raw
raw.description:
Wraps a plain style object as a utility mixin, so bespoke declarations — a
property outside this package's surface, or a call-site-computed value —
compose inside wrappers like `when()`, whose inputs are utility mixins.
raw.summary: Wraps a plain style object as a utility mixin, so bespoke declarations — a property outside this package's surface, or a call-site-computed value — compose inside wrappers like `when()`, whose inputs are utility mixins.

touchAction.name: touchAction
touchAction.description:
Applies `touch-action`. Defaults to `"none"`, the common case of a custom
drag handle or gesture surface that handles its own touch input.

userSelect.name: userSelect
userSelect.description:
Applies `user-select`. Defaults to `"none"`, the common case of a label,
icon, or drag handle that stays clear of highlight through an incidental
click-drag.

var.name: var
var.description:
Resolves a custom property reference: `var(--{name})`, or with a fallback,
`var(--{name}, {fallback})`. `name` omits the leading `--`, matching
`u.vars()`; the raw string fits anywhere a utility takes a CSS value.
var.summary: Resolves a custom property reference: `var(--{name})`, or with a fallback, `var(--{name}, {fallback})`.

vars.name: vars
vars.description:
Sets custom properties on the host element, with the leading `--` omitted
from each key so call sites read as plain option names.
vars.summary: Sets custom properties on the host element, with the leading `--` omitted from each key so call sites read as plain option names.

willChange.name: willChange
willChange.description:
Applies `will-change`, hinting the browser to optimize for an upcoming
animation on the given property/properties before it starts.
willChange.summary: Applies `will-change`, hinting the browser to optimize for an upcoming animation on the given property/properties before it starts.

anchor.name: anchor
anchor.description:
Resolves an `anchor()` reference to a plain string — the length an inset
utility needs to pin an edge to the anchor's geometry. The leading `--` is
prepended; `fallback` keeps the inset valid when no anchor resolves.
anchor.summary: Resolves an `anchor()` reference to a plain string — the length an inset utility needs to pin an edge to the anchor's geometry.
anchor.signature: u.anchor(name: string, side: AnchorSide, fallback?: string)

anchorName.name: anchorName
anchorName.description:
Applies `anchor-name`, the *declaring* half of anchor positioning: it goes
on the element anchored **to**, and positionAnchor points back at
this name. The leading `--` is prepended — an anchor name is a dashed-ident.
anchorName.summary: Applies `anchor-name`, the *declaring* half of anchor positioning: it goes on the element anchored **to**, and positionAnchor points back at this name.

anchorSize.name: anchorSize
anchorSize.description:
Resolves an `anchor-size()` reference to a plain string, letting a panel
track its trigger's size in one browser-maintained declaration. The leading
`--` is prepended; `fallback` keeps it valid when no anchor resolves.
anchorSize.summary: Resolves an `anchor-size()` reference to a plain string, letting a panel track its trigger's size in one browser-maintained declaration.
anchorSize.signature: u.anchorSize(name: string, dimension: AnchorSizeDimension, fallback?: string)

appearance.name: appearance
appearance.description:
Applies `appearance` to clear a form control's native platform chrome, which
Safari and Firefox honor only with their own prefixed property alongside the
standard one, so all three are emitted; `options` narrows that set.
appearance.summary: Applies `appearance` to clear a form control's native platform chrome, which Safari and Firefox honor only with their own prefixed property alongside the standard one, so all three are emitted; `options` narrows that set.

examples.call: u.appearance("none", { moz: false }) // Chromium/Safari-only vendor reset

basis.name: basis
basis.description:
Applies `flex-basis`, defaulting to `"auto"` to match the property's own
initial value — the remainder of a `flex: N N M` shorthand once
`u.grow()`/`u.shrink()` have been extracted from it.
basis.summary: Applies `flex-basis`, defaulting to `"auto"` to match the property's own initial value — the remainder of a `flex: N N M` shorthand once `u.grow()`/`u.shrink()` have been extracted from it.

borderCollapse.name: borderCollapse
borderCollapse.description:
Applies `border-collapse`. Defaults to `"collapse"`, the common case of a
table whose cell borders should merge into single lines instead of
doubling up.

borderSpacing.name: borderSpacing
borderSpacing.description:
Applies the `border-spacing` property — the gap between adjacent table
cell borders when `border-collapse: separate` is in effect (its default).
borderSpacing.summary: Applies the `border-spacing` property — the gap between adjacent table cell borders when `border-collapse: separate` is in effect (its default).

boxSizing.name: boxSizing
boxSizing.description:
Applies `box-sizing`, controlling whether `width`/`height` (and the logical
`inline-size`/`block-size` pair) span padding and border (`"border-box"`) or
the content area alone (`"content-box"`, the CSS default).
boxSizing.summary: Applies `box-sizing`, controlling whether `width`/`height` (and the logical `inline-size`/`block-size` pair) span padding and border (`"border-box"`) or the content area alone (`"content-box"`, the CSS default).

center.name: center
center.description:
A zero-argument convenience pattern that centers content both ways.
Composes `u.flex()`, `u.items("center")`, and `u.justify("center")`, so its
output is exactly the declarations those three produce.
center.summary: A zero-argument convenience pattern that centers content both ways.

contain.name: contain
contain.description:
Applies `contain`, letting the browser skip layout and paint work it can
prove stays inside the subtree. Defaults to `"content"`; every value beyond
`"none"` makes the element a containing block and a stacking context.
contain.summary: Applies `contain`, letting the browser skip layout and paint work it can prove stays inside the subtree.

container.name: container
container.description:
Declares the host as a named container query context via the `container`
shorthand (`container-name` and `container-type` together), so a
descendant's `u.at(size, name, ...)` query can target it by name.
container.summary: Declares the host as a named container query context via the `container` shorthand (`container-name` and `container-type` together), so a descendant's `u.at(size, name, ...)` query can target it by name.

content.name: content
content.description:
Sets `align-content`, using the same accepted keywords and
`between`/`around`/`evenly` aliasing as `u.justify()`.
content.summary: Sets `align-content`, using the same accepted keywords and `between`/`around`/`evenly` aliasing as `u.justify()`.

contents.name: contents
contents.description:
Sets `display: contents`, removing the host element's own box so its
children participate directly in the parent's layout.
contents.summary: Sets `display: contents`, removing the host element's own box so its children participate directly in the parent's layout.

contentVisibility.name: contentVisibility
contentVisibility.description:
Applies `content-visibility` so the browser skips rendering work for an
element's contents; defaults to `"auto"`. Long scrollable lists want
virtualize, which also reserves a placeholder size for the scrollbar.
contentVisibility.summary: Applies `content-visibility` so the browser skips rendering work for an element's contents; defaults to `"auto"`.

fieldSizing.name: fieldSizing
fieldSizing.description:
Applies `field-sizing` to an `<input>`, `<textarea>`, or `<select>`.
Defaults to `"content"`, sizing the control to the value it holds; cap that
growth with `u.maxBs()` or `u.maxIs()` so overflow takes over past the cap.

gap.name: gap
gap.description:
Applies `gap` using the spacing scale or a raw CSS length. One value
applies to both the row and column gap; two values are read as
`"{row} {column}"`.
gap.summary: Applies `gap` using the spacing scale or a raw CSS length.

gridArea.name: gridArea
gridArea.description:
Applies `grid-area`, placing an element in a named area of its parent's
`grid-template-areas`.
gridArea.summary: Applies `grid-area`, placing an element in a named area of its parent's `grid-template-areas`.

gridAutoColumns.name: gridAutoColumns
gridAutoColumns.description:
Applies `grid-auto-columns` to the *implicit* columns a grid creates past
its explicit tracks. A number resolves on the spacing scale, `"full"` to
`100%`; raw strings such as `minmax(...)` reach CSS verbatim.
gridAutoColumns.summary: Applies `grid-auto-columns` to the *implicit* columns a grid creates past its explicit tracks.

gridAutoFlow.name: gridAutoFlow
gridAutoFlow.description:
Applies `grid-auto-flow`, the axis auto-placed items fill along; defaults
to `"row"`. `dense` backfills earlier holes with later items, diverging
visual order from the DOM order focus follows — keep it presentational.
gridAutoFlow.summary: Applies `grid-auto-flow`, the axis auto-placed items fill along; defaults to `"row"`.

gridAutoRows.name: gridAutoRows
gridAutoRows.description:
Applies `grid-auto-rows` to the *implicit* rows a grid creates past its
explicit tracks. A number resolves on the spacing scale, `"full"` to
`100%`; raw strings such as `minmax(...)` reach CSS verbatim.
gridAutoRows.summary: Applies `grid-auto-rows` to the *implicit* rows a grid creates past its explicit tracks.

gridColumn.name: gridColumn
gridColumn.description:
Applies `grid-column`, shorthand for `grid-column-start` /
`grid-column-end`: one value sets the start line and spans one track, a
`"start / end"` string sets both. A number always reads as a line number.
gridColumn.summary: Applies `grid-column`, shorthand for `grid-column-start` / `grid-column-end`: one value sets the start line and spans one track, a `"start / end"` string sets both.

gridRow.name: gridRow
gridRow.description:
Applies `grid-row`, placing or spanning a grid item along the block axis. A
number is a line number: `u.gridRow(2)` starts the item at the second row
line and occupies one track, while `u.gridRow("span 2")` occupies two.
gridRow.summary: Applies `grid-row`, placing or spanning a grid item along the block axis.

gridTemplate.name: gridTemplate
gridTemplate.description:
Applies `grid-template-columns`/`-rows`/`-areas` from whichever option keys
are given. Track lists vary too continuously for a named scale, so values
are raw CSS strings; repeat builds the `repeat(count, track)` shape.
gridTemplate.summary: Applies `grid-template-columns`/`-rows`/`-areas` from whichever option keys are given.

grow.name: grow
grow.description:
Applies `flex-grow`. Defaults to `1`, the common case of a flexible item —
a content area next to a fixed-size sidebar or icon — that should expand
to fill whatever room is left in its flex container.

hidden.name: hidden
hidden.description: Sets `display: none`, removing the host element from layout entirely.
hidden.summary: Sets `display: none`, removing the host element from layout entirely.

hstack.name: hstack
hstack.description:
A horizontal flex stack. Composes `u.flex()`, `u.flexRow()`, and — from
whichever option keys are given — `u.gap()`, `u.items()`, and
`u.justify()`.

examples.output: css({ display: "flex", flexDirection: "row", gap: "calc(var(--ui-spacing, 0.25rem) * 4)", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "space-between" })

insBe.name: insBe
insBe.description:
Applies `inset-block-end` — the trailing block edge, the bottom edge in a
horizontal writing mode.
insBe.summary: Applies `inset-block-end` — the trailing block edge, the bottom edge in a horizontal writing mode.

insBottom.name: insBottom
insBottom.description:
Applies the physical `bottom` property. Reach for it when the offset is
genuinely tied to the physical bottom side; `u.insBe()`
(`inset-block-end`) covers the logical block edge.

insBs.name: insBs
insBs.description:
Applies `inset-block-start` — the leading block edge, the top edge in a
horizontal writing mode.
insBs.summary: Applies `inset-block-start` — the leading block edge, the top edge in a horizontal writing mode.

inset.name: inset
inset.description:
Applies a logical `inset` shorthand from the spacing scale or a raw CSS
length. One value covers every side; two map to block then inline; four
map to block-start, inline-end, block-end, inline-start.
inset.summary: Applies a logical `inset` shorthand from the spacing scale or a raw CSS length.

insIe.name: insIe
insIe.description:
Applies `inset-inline-end` — the trailing inline edge, which is the right
edge in `ltr` and the left edge in `rtl`.
insIe.summary: Applies `inset-inline-end` — the trailing inline edge, which is the right edge in `ltr` and the left edge in `rtl`.

insIs.name: insIs
insIs.description:
Applies `inset-inline-start` — the leading inline edge, which is the left
edge in `ltr` and the right edge in `rtl`.
insIs.summary: Applies `inset-inline-start` — the leading inline edge, which is the left edge in `ltr` and the right edge in `rtl`.

insLeft.name: insLeft
insLeft.description:
Applies the physical `left` property, for offsets genuinely tied to the
viewport's left side. `u.insIs()` (`inset-inline-start`) covers the
writing-direction-aware default.
insLeft.summary: Applies the physical `left` property, for offsets genuinely tied to the viewport's left side.

insRight.name: insRight
insRight.description:
Applies the physical `right` property, for offsets genuinely tied to the
viewport's right side. `u.insIe()` (`inset-inline-end`) covers the
writing-direction-aware default.
insRight.summary: Applies the physical `right` property, for offsets genuinely tied to the viewport's right side.

insTop.name: insTop
insTop.description:
Applies the physical `top` property, for offsets genuinely tied to the
viewport's top side. `u.insBs()` (`inset-block-start`) covers the
writing-direction-aware default.
insTop.summary: Applies the physical `top` property, for offsets genuinely tied to the viewport's top side.

interpolateSize.name: interpolateSize
interpolateSize.description:
Opts the element into animating to and from keyword sizes (`auto`,
`min-content`, `max-content`, `fit-content`), so a transition to
`height: auto` or `block-size: auto` animates across its full duration.
interpolateSize.summary: Opts the element into animating to and from keyword sizes (`auto`, `min-content`, `max-content`, `fit-content`), so a transition to `height: auto` or `block-size: auto` animates across its full duration.

justify.name: justify
justify.description:
Sets `justify-content`, aliasing the short `between`/`around`/`evenly`
forms to their `space-*` CSS keywords.
justify.summary: Sets `justify-content`, aliasing the short `between`/`around`/`evenly` forms to their `space-*` CSS keywords.

place.name: place
place.description:
Sets item and/or content placement on both axes from whichever option
keys are given, so a partial options object emits only the declarations
belonging to the keys it carries.
place.summary: Sets item and/or content placement on both axes from whichever option keys are given, so a partial options object emits only the declarations belonging to the keys it carries.

positionAnchor.name: positionAnchor
positionAnchor.description:
Points an absolutely or fixed positioned element (a tooltip, popover, or
menu) at the anchor name anchorName declared on its target. Pass
`name` bare; the `--` custom-property prefix is added here.
positionAnchor.summary: Points an absolutely or fixed positioned element (a tooltip, popover, or menu) at the anchor name anchorName declared on its target.

positionArea.name: positionArea
positionArea.description:
Applies the CSS Anchor Positioning `position-area` property, placing an
anchor-positioned element in a named region of the 3x3 grid around its
anchor. Accepts the whole logical-position-keyword grammar as a string.
positionArea.summary: Applies the CSS Anchor Positioning `position-area` property, placing an anchor-positioned element in a named region of the 3x3 grid around its anchor.

positionTryFallbacks.name: positionTryFallbacks
positionTryFallbacks.description:
Applies the CSS Anchor Positioning `position-try-fallbacks` property,
listing named tactics or `--custom-position-try` references tried in order
when the preferred position overflows its containing block.
positionTryFallbacks.summary: Applies the CSS Anchor Positioning `position-try-fallbacks` property, listing named tactics or `--custom-position-try` references tried in order when the preferred position overflows its containing block.

repeat.name: repeat
repeat.description:
Builds a `repeat(...)` track-list value string for `u.gridTemplate()`'s
`columns`/`rows` options, or any `grid-template-columns`/`-rows` use, since
track sizing varies too continuously for a named scale to usefully cover.
repeat.summary: Builds a `repeat(...)` track-list value string for `u.gridTemplate()`'s `columns`/`rows` options, or any `grid-template-columns`/`-rows` use, since track sizing varies too continuously for a named scale to usefully cover.

resize.name: resize
resize.description:
Applies `resize`, controlling which axes a user can drag the element's
resize handle along. Defaults to `"block"`, the shape most textareas want,
and only takes effect on an element whose `overflow` is not `visible`.
resize.summary: Applies `resize`, controlling which axes a user can drag the element's resize handle along.

shrink.name: shrink
shrink.description:
Applies `flex-shrink`. Defaults to `0`, the common case of a fixed-size
flex item — an icon or graphic slot — that keeps its size alongside the
flexible content next to it.

spacer.name: spacer
spacer.description:
A flexible spacer: grows and shrinks to fill whatever room is left in a
flex container, pushing siblings on either side of it apart — a toolbar's
trailing action pinned to the end, or two row groups split to the edges.
spacer.summary: A flexible spacer: grows and shrinks to fill whatever room is left in a flex container, pushing siblings on either side of it apart — a toolbar's trailing action pinned to the end, or two row groups split to the edges.

virtualize.name: virtualize
virtualize.description:
Applies `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size` so the
browser skips rendering off-screen rows in a long list or table, using
`intrinsicSize` as a placeholder so the scrollbar doesn't jump on mount.
virtualize.summary: Applies `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size` so the browser skips rendering off-screen rows in a long list or table, using `intrinsicSize` as a placeholder so the scrollbar doesn't jump on mount.

vstack.name: vstack
vstack.description:
A vertical flex stack. Composes `u.flex()`, `u.flexCol()`, and — from
whichever option keys are given — `u.gap()`, `u.items()`, and
`u.justify()`.

zstack.name: zstack
zstack.description:
A grid-overlay stack for layering children on top of each other. Composes
`u.grid()` and, when given, `u.items()` for `align-items`; `justify-items`
has no dedicated utility, so it's set directly.
zstack.summary: A grid-overlay stack for layering children on top of each other.

accent.name: accent
accent.description:
Applies `accent-color`, the property native form controls (`checkbox`,
`radio`, `range`, `progress`) read for their own painted color. Defaults
to the brand solid color so a bare `u.accent()` always resolves.
accent.summary: Applies `accent-color`, the property native form controls (`checkbox`, `radio`, `range`, `progress`) read for their own painted color.

autofill.name: autofill
autofill.description:
Overrides the browser's autofill background and text color under
`&:-webkit-autofill`, so an autofilled input keeps the appearance every
other input has. Defaults to the system background/foreground tokens.
autofill.summary: Overrides the browser's autofill background and text color under `&:-webkit-autofill`, so an autofilled input keeps the appearance every other input has.

examples.output: css({ "&:-webkit-autofill": { boxShadow: "0 0 0 1000px var(--ui-bg, Canvas) inset !important", WebkitBoxShadow: "0 0 0 1000px var(--ui-bg, Canvas) inset !important", WebkitTextFillColor: "var(--ui-fg, CanvasText) !important" } })

bg.name: bg
bg.description:
Applies `background-color`, or the full set of background properties when
given an options object, of which only the given keys are set. A semantic
tone requires a `tint`/`solid` suffix so the call site states its weight.
bg.summary: Applies `background-color`, or the full set of background properties when given an options object, of which only the given keys are set.

border.name: border
border.description:
Applies `border-color`, or the full set of border properties when given an
options object, of which only the given keys are set. A bare tone resolves
its plain `border` weight, which the theme promotes under high contrast.
border.summary: Applies `border-color`, or the full set of border properties when given an options object, of which only the given keys are set.

examples.output: css({ borderColor: "var(--ui-border, color-mix(in oklab, CanvasText 16%, transparent))" })

borderEdge.name: borderEdge
borderEdge.description:
Applies a border to a single edge only, for a divider between two adjacent
elements (e.g. two stepper buttons sharing one frame). Only the given keys
are set; prefer a logical edge so the divider follows writing mode.
borderEdge.summary: Applies a border to a single edge only, for a divider between two adjacent elements (e.g.

caretColor.name: caretColor
caretColor.description:
Sets `caret-color` for an editable field, resolving a tone at its `fg`
weight. With no value it emits `"auto"`, deriving the caret from the
field's text color; pass a tone when that reads near-invisible on a tint.
caretColor.summary: Sets `caret-color` for an editable field, resolving a tone at its `fg` weight.

colorMix.name: colorMix
colorMix.description:
Builds a `color-mix(...)` value string for any color-accepting property.
`colorSpace` is the raw interpolation space CSS expects (`"oklab"`,
`"srgb"`, `"hsl"`, ...).
colorMix.summary: Builds a `color-mix(...)` value string for any color-accepting property.

colorScheme.name: colorScheme
colorScheme.description:
Sets `color-scheme`, which tells the browser which schemes an element
renders correctly in, so the chrome the browser paints itself — scrollbars,
pickers, form controls — follows the theme. It inherits: set it on `<html>`.
colorScheme.summary: Sets `color-scheme`, which tells the browser which schemes an element renders correctly in, so the chrome the browser paints itself — scrollbars, pickers, form controls — follows the theme.

conicGradient.name: conicGradient
conicGradient.description:
Builds a `conic-gradient(...)` value string for any `background-image` use.
A numeric `angle` is treated as degrees and wrapped in the `from` keyword
CSS requires; a string passes through as the full `from ... at ...` clause.
conicGradient.summary: Builds a `conic-gradient(...)` value string for any `background-image` use.

fg.name: fg
fg.description:
Applies `color` (foreground text color). Called with no value it resolves
the tiny system default (`var(--ui-fg, CanvasText)`); called with a bare
tone it defaults to that tone's plain `fg` weight.

fill.name: fill
fill.description:
Applies the SVG `fill` paint property, resolving semantic tones the same way
`color` does. With no value it resolves the system default
(`var(--ui-fg, CanvasText)`); a bare tone resolves that tone's `fg` weight.
fill.summary: Applies the SVG `fill` paint property, resolving semantic tones the same way `color` does.

fillOpacity.name: fillOpacity
fillOpacity.description:
Sets the SVG `fill-opacity` paint property. A bare number is read as a 0-100
integer, matching `u.opacity()`. The ratio is stringified because the
serializer appends `px`, and `fill-opacity: 0.5px` is dropped as invalid.

linearGradient.name: linearGradient
linearGradient.description:
Builds a `linear-gradient(...)` value string for any `background-image` use.
A numeric `angle` is treated as degrees; a string passes through unchanged,
so CSS's own side/corner keywords work too.
linearGradient.summary: Builds a `linear-gradient(...)` value string for any `background-image` use.

outline.name: outline
outline.description:
Applies an outline unconditionally, for a persistent or decorative edge. A
bare string is a color, a bare number is a width in pixels, the two together
set both, and an options object sets every property at once.
outline.summary: Applies an outline unconditionally, for a persistent or decorative edge.

outlineColor.name: outlineColor
outlineColor.description:
Sets `outline-color` alone, so a state such as `[aria-invalid]` can tint an
outline while the width and style already in effect stay in force. With no
argument it resolves the system default ring color.
outlineColor.summary: Sets `outline-color` alone, so a state such as `[aria-invalid]` can tint an outline while the width and style already in effect stay in force.

outlineStyle.name: outlineStyle
outlineStyle.description:
Sets `outline-style` alone, so a state can override the style while the
color and width already in effect stay in force.
outlineStyle.summary: Sets `outline-style` alone, so a state can override the style while the color and width already in effect stay in force.

outlineWidth.name: outlineWidth
outlineWidth.description:
Sets `outline-width` alone, so a state can override the width while the
color and style already in effect stay in force. A bare number is treated
as pixels; a string passes through unchanged.
outlineWidth.summary: Sets `outline-width` alone, so a state can override the width while the color and style already in effect stay in force.

radialGradient.name: radialGradient
radialGradient.description:
Builds a `radial-gradient(...)` value string for any `background-image` use.
`shape` is the raw shape/size/position clause CSS expects, so a compound
clause such as `"ellipse at top left"` passes through unchanged.
radialGradient.summary: Builds a `radial-gradient(...)` value string for any `background-image` use.

examples.call: u.radialGradient("circle at top left", { color: "red", position: "20%" }, "blue")

ring.name: ring
ring.description:
Applies a focus ring already scoped to `&:focus-visible`, so it shows for
keyboard and assistive-tech focus and a component can apply it directly.
ring.summary: Applies a focus ring already scoped to `&:focus-visible`, so it shows for keyboard and assistive-tech focus and a component can apply it directly.

examples.output: css({ "&:focus-visible": { outlineWidth: "2px", outlineStyle: "solid", outlineOffset: "2px", outlineColor: "var(--ui-ring, Highlight)" } })

stroke.name: stroke
stroke.description:
Applies `stroke`, resolving a semantic tone to an SVG shape's outline
color. With no value it resolves the system default
`var(--ui-fg, CanvasText)`; a bare tone resolves that tone's `fg` weight.
stroke.summary: Applies `stroke`, resolving a semantic tone to an SVG shape's outline color.

strokeLinecap.name: strokeLinecap
strokeLinecap.description:
Sets `stroke-linecap`, the SVG paint property controlling how a
`<path>`/`<line>` shape's stroke renders at the two open ends of an
unclosed subpath.
strokeLinecap.summary: Sets `stroke-linecap`, the SVG paint property controlling how a `<path>`/`<line>` shape's stroke renders at the two open ends of an unclosed subpath.

strokeLinejoin.name: strokeLinejoin
strokeLinejoin.description:
Sets `stroke-linejoin`, the SVG paint property controlling how a
`<path>`/`<polyline>`/`<polygon>` shape's stroke renders at a corner
between two segments.
strokeLinejoin.summary: Sets `stroke-linejoin`, the SVG paint property controlling how a `<path>`/`<polyline>`/`<polygon>` shape's stroke renders at a corner between two segments.

strokeWidth.name: strokeWidth
strokeWidth.description:
Sets `stroke-width` on an SVG shape. A bare number stays a unitless SVG
user-unit value, so the stroke scales with the SVG's own coordinate
system; a string passes through for a value that needs an explicit unit.

surface.name: surface
surface.description:
Composes `u.bg()`, `u.fg()`, and `u.border()` so a surface's contrast holds
by construction. Accepts recipe names only, because a surface's background,
foreground, and border must be chosen as one matching set.
surface.summary: Composes `u.bg()`, `u.fg()`, and `u.border()` so a surface's contrast holds by construction.

examples.output: css({ backgroundColor: "var(--ui-bg, Canvas)", color: "var(--ui-fg, CanvasText)", borderColor: "var(--ui-border, ...)" })

translucent.name: translucent
translucent.description:
A solid background plus backdrop blur, gated behind
`prefers-reduced-transparency: no-preference` so a reduced-transparency
preference keeps the plain solid background and stays legible.
translucent.summary: A solid background plus backdrop blur, gated behind `prefers-reduced-transparency: no-preference` so a reduced-transparency preference keeps the plain solid background and stays legible.

examples.output: css({ backgroundColor: "var(--ui-bg, Canvas)", "@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: no-preference)": { "--ui-backdrop-blur": "var(--ui-blur-sm, 4px)", backdropFilter: "blur(var(--ui-backdrop-blur, 0px)) ...", WebkitBackdropFilter: "blur(var(--ui-backdrop-blur, 0px)) ..." } })

vectorEffect.name: vectorEffect
vectorEffect.description:
Sets `vector-effect`, exempting an SVG shape from its ancestor transforms:
`"non-scaling-stroke"` keeps a chart line's stroke width constant while the
chart itself scales or zooms.
vectorEffect.summary: Sets `vector-effect`, exempting an SVG shape from its ancestor transforms: `"non-scaling-stroke"` keeps a chart line's stroke width constant while the chart itself scales or zooms.

isolate.name: isolate
isolate.description:
Creates a new stacking context on the host element while preserving its
layout, so a later `z-index` on this element (or a descendant) stays
confined here, isolated from unrelated siblings outside it.
isolate.summary: Creates a new stacking context on the host element while preserving its layout, so a later `z-index` on this element (or a descendant) stays confined here, isolated from unrelated siblings outside it.

layer.name: layer
layer.description:
Composes isolate and z so a single call gets both a new
stacking context and a stacking order. Accepts only numeric values,
leaving named layers like `"toast"` or `"modal"` to app or component code.
layer.summary: Composes isolate and z so a single call gets both a new stacking context and a stacking order.

z.name: z
z.description:
Sets the host element's `z-index` from a plain number. Named component
layers such as `"toast"` or `"modal"` are an app or component concern,
so this primitive stays scoped to raw numeric values.
z.summary: Sets the host element's `z-index` from a plain number.

animation.name: animation
animation.description:
Emits an `@keyframes` rule under `name` together with the host
`animation-*` declarations that reference it. Use the named form when the
animation name is useful for debugging in devtools.
animation.summary: Emits an `@keyframes` rule under `name` together with the host `animation-*` declarations that reference it.

animationDelay.name: animationDelay
animationDelay.description:
Applies the `animation-delay` property. The value is a `<time>` string, so
it always carries its unit, and a negative delay seeks: the animation starts
immediately, already advanced by that much of its duration.

animationHost.name: animationHost
animationHost.description:
Emits the host `animation-*` declarations alone, taking every
AnimationConfig key but `keyframes`. Pair it with a sibling
`u.keyframes` call, since `@keyframes` only hoists from a mixin's top level.
animationHost.summary: Emits the host `animation-*` declarations alone, taking every AnimationConfig key but `keyframes`.

examples.call:
<div
  mix={[
    u.keyframes("ui-spin-rotate", { from: { transform: "rotate(0deg)" }, to: { transform: "rotate(360deg)" } }),
    u.when("&[data-busy]", u.animationHost("ui-spin-rotate", { duration: "1s", iterationCount: "infinite" })),
  ]}
/>

keyframes.name: keyframes
keyframes.description:
Emits an `@keyframes` rule under `name` at the top level, where the
serializer reads stop keys (`from`, `to`, `50%`) as stop selectors. Pair it
with a `css()` call that sets `animationName` and `animationDuration`.
keyframes.summary: Emits an `@keyframes` rule under `name` at the top level, where the serializer reads stop keys (`from`, `to`, `50%`) as stop selectors.

examples.call:
<div
  mix={[
    u.keyframes("fade-in", {
      from: { opacity: 0 },
      to: { opacity: 1 },
    }),
    css({
      animationName: "fade-in",
      animationDuration: "150ms",
    }),
  ]}
/>

// Equivalent at the top level of a `css()` call.
css({ "@keyframes fade-in": { from: { opacity: 0 }, to: { opacity: 1 } } })

scrollTimelineName.name: scrollTimelineName
scrollTimelineName.description:
Applies `scroll-timeline-name` to the scroll container itself, which needs
an `overflow` value that scrolls. The leading `--` is added here, and the
animation references the literal dashed-ident: `timeline: "--{name}"`.
scrollTimelineName.summary: Applies `scroll-timeline-name` to the scroll container itself, which needs an `overflow` value that scrolls.

timelineScope.name: timelineScope
timelineScope.description:
Applies the `timeline-scope` property, raising a named timeline's
visibility to a common ancestor's subtree so animations outside the
declaring element can resolve the name; the subtree still declares it.
timelineScope.summary: Applies the `timeline-scope` property, raising a named timeline's visibility to a common ancestor's subtree so animations outside the declaring element can resolve the name; the subtree still declares it.

viewTimelineName.name: viewTimelineName
viewTimelineName.description:
Applies `view-timeline-name` to the element being *watched* — the card, the
section, the image. The leading `--` is added here, and the animation
references the literal dashed-ident: `timeline: "--{name}"`.
viewTimelineName.summary: Applies `view-timeline-name` to the element being *watched* — the card, the section, the image.

after.name: after
after.description:
Applies the given utilities to an element's `::after` pseudo-element.
Sugar over `when("&::after", input)`.
after.summary: Applies the given utilities to an element's `::after` pseudo-element.

aria.name: aria
aria.description:
Sugar over `when(...)` for an element's `aria-*` attribute selector: two
args match the attribute present with any value — including `"false"` —
while three args match a value exactly; pass `"true"` for the truthy case.
aria.summary: Sugar over `when(...)` for an element's `aria-*` attribute selector: two args match the attribute present with any value — including `"false"` — while three args match a value exactly; pass `"true"` for the truthy case.

backdrop.name: backdrop
backdrop.description:
Applies the given utilities to a top-layer element's `::backdrop`, the
layer the browser paints behind a `<dialog>` or popover to dim the page
with no overlay, z-index, or scroll container; pairs with `u.open()`.
backdrop.summary: Applies the given utilities to a top-layer element's `::backdrop`, the layer the browser paints behind a `<dialog>` or popover to dim the page with no overlay, z-index, or scroll container; pairs with `u.open()`.

before.name: before
before.description:
Applies the given utilities to an element's `::before` pseudo-element.
Sugar over `when("&::before", input)`.
before.summary: Applies the given utilities to an element's `::before` pseudo-element.

checked.name: checked
checked.description:
Sugar over `when('&:checked, &[aria-checked="true"]', input)`, matching
both native checked controls and ARIA-checked custom widgets.
checked.summary: Sugar over `when('&:checked, &[aria-checked="true"]', input)`, matching both native checked controls and ARIA-checked custom widgets.

data.name: data
data.description:
Sugar over an element's own `data-*` attribute selector: matches
`&[data-{attribute}]` (any value, including a bare boolean attribute) with no
`value` argument, or `&[data-{attribute}="{value}"]` with one.
data.summary: Sugar over an element's own `data-*` attribute selector: matches `&[data-{attribute}]` (any value, including a bare boolean attribute) with no `value` argument, or `&[data-{attribute}="{value}"]` with one.

detailsContent.name: detailsContent
detailsContent.description:
Applies the given utilities to a `<details>` element's `::details-content`
pseudo-element, the region holding everything after the `<summary>`.
Combine with `u.open()`'s selector to scope styles to the open state.
detailsContent.summary: Applies the given utilities to a `<details>` element's `::details-content` pseudo-element, the region holding everything after the `<summary>`.

disabled.name: disabled
disabled.description:
Sugar over `when('&:disabled, &[aria-disabled="true"]', input)`, applying
the given utilities under both the native and ARIA disabled selectors.
Callers choose the actual colors, opacity, and cursor for that state.
disabled.summary: Sugar over `when('&:disabled, &[aria-disabled="true"]', input)`, applying the given utilities under both the native and ARIA disabled selectors.

has.name: has
has.description:
Sugar over `when("&:has({selector})", input)`. Styles an element by its own
descendants' state; `:has()` takes the specificity of its heaviest argument,
so a complex selector here can outweigh overriding declarations.

hasSibling.name: hasSibling
hasSibling.description:
Sugar over `when("&:has(~ {selector})", input)`, styling an element by a
sibling's state. `~` matches only *following* siblings, so the indicator
must come before the source input in the DOM.
hasSibling.summary: Sugar over `when("&:has(~ {selector})", input)`, styling an element by a sibling's state.

indeterminate.name: indeterminate
indeterminate.description:
Matches indeterminate checkboxes and ARIA mixed-state widgets, painting a
third visual state; it also matches radios in an unselected group and
valueless `<progress>`, so scope it to the control you mean.
indeterminate.summary: Matches indeterminate checkboxes and ARIA mixed-state widgets, painting a third visual state; it also matches radios in an unselected group and valueless `<progress>`, so scope it to the control you mean.

invalid.name: invalid
invalid.description:
Waits for user interaction before flagging a field invalid, matching
`:user-invalid` alongside the ARIA fallback so validation only surfaces
once it is meaningful to the person filling in the field.
invalid.summary: Waits for user interaction before flagging a field invalid, matching `:user-invalid` alongside the ARIA fallback so validation only surfaces once it is meaningful to the person filling in the field.

marker.name: marker
marker.description:
Applies the given utilities to a list item's marker or a `<summary>`
disclosure triangle via `::marker`; only `color`, `font-*`, and `content`
apply. Use `u.listStyle("none")` to remove the marker along with its space.
marker.summary: Applies the given utilities to a list item's marker or a `<summary>` disclosure triangle via `::marker`; only `color`, `font-*`, and `content` apply.

not.name: not
not.description:
A selector wrapper for negated state: wraps `selector` in `:not(...)` and
applies the given utilities there.
not.summary: A selector wrapper for negated state: wraps `selector` in `:not(...)` and applies the given utilities there.

open.name: open
open.description:
Sugar over `when("&[open], &:popover-open", input)`, matching both the
`<details>`/`<dialog>` `open` attribute and the Popover API's
`:popover-open` pseudo-class.
open.summary: Sugar over `when("&[open], &:popover-open", input)`, matching both the `<details>`/`<dialog>` `open` attribute and the Popover API's `:popover-open` pseudo-class.

placeholder.name: placeholder
placeholder.description:
Styles an input or textarea's `::placeholder` text. Give the field a real
`<label>` too, since placeholder text vanishes on input and often renders
at low contrast; style the empty input itself with `u.placeholderShown()`.
placeholder.summary: Styles an input or textarea's `::placeholder` text.

placeholderShown.name: placeholderShown
placeholderShown.description:
Sugar over `when("&:placeholder-shown", input)`, matching an input or
textarea while it is empty and therefore still showing its placeholder.
Enables the float-label pattern with no JavaScript, paired with `u.has()`.
placeholderShown.summary: Sugar over `when("&:placeholder-shown", input)`, matching an input or textarea while it is empty and therefore still showing its placeholder.

precededBy.name: precededBy
precededBy.description:
Sugar over `when(":is({selector}) ~ &", input)`, the backward-looking twin
of `hasSibling()`. The `:is()` wrapper is load-bearing: the serializer reads
a bare `input:checked ~ &` key as a declaration, so wrapping keeps it a rule.
precededBy.summary: Sugar over `when(":is({selector}) ~ &", input)`, the backward-looking twin of `hasSibling()`.

readOnly.name: readOnly
readOnly.description:
Sugar over `when('&:read-only, &[aria-readonly="true"]', input)`, matching
native and ARIA read-only controls. They stay focusable and keep submitting
their value with the form, so give them a flat, normal-but-static style.
readOnly.summary: Sugar over `when('&:read-only, &[aria-readonly="true"]', input)`, matching native and ARIA read-only controls.

required.name: required
required.description:
Sugar over `when('&:required, &[aria-required="true"]', input)`, matching
required controls and widgets. Add a textual cue in the label too, since
colour and a bare asterisk alone only reach sighted users.
required.summary: Sugar over `when('&:required, &[aria-required="true"]', input)`, matching required controls and widgets.

selection.name: selection
selection.description:
Applies utilities to the element's `::selection`; only `color`,
`background-color`, `text-decoration`, and `text-shadow` take effect, and
overriding the platform's contrast guarantee requires a high-contrast pair.
selection.summary: Applies utilities to the element's `::selection`; only `color`, `background-color`, `text-decoration`, and `text-shadow` take effect, and overriding the platform's contrast guarantee requires a high-contrast pair.

when.name: when
when.description:
The primitive selector wrapper every other state wrapper (`hover()`,
`checked()`, ...) is sugar over. `selector` must start with `&`, `@`, `:`,
`[`, or `.`; see checkNestedSelector for what happens otherwise.
when.summary: The primitive selector wrapper every other state wrapper (`hover()`, `checked()`, ...) is sugar over.

where.name: where
where.description:
Sugar over `when("& :where({selector})", input)`, targeting descendants of
the host. `:where()` always contributes zero specificity, so the resulting
rule stays overridable by any later single-class rule.
where.summary: Sugar over `when("& :where({selector})", input)`, targeting descendants of the host.

clip.name: clip
clip.description:
Applies `overflow: clip`, the modern alternative to `overflow: hidden`.
Overflow stays permanently unreachable: user input, programmatic scrolling,
and focusing a clipped descendant all leave the element unscrolled.
clip.summary: Applies `overflow: clip`, the modern alternative to `overflow: hidden`.

divide.name: divide
divide.description:
Applies a divider border between every child except the last, along `axis`.
A number in the color position is read as the border width, so a width can
be set alone; a color name resolves through the semantic and palette tokens.
divide.summary: Applies a divider border between every child except the last, along `axis`.
divide.signature: u.divide(axis?: DivideAxis, colorOrWidth?: ColorValue | (string & {}) | number, maybeWidth?: number)

examples.output: css({ "& > *:not(:last-child)": { borderStyle: "solid", borderBlockEndWidth: "1px", borderBlockEndColor: "var(--ui-border, color-mix(in oklab, CanvasText 16%, transparent))" } })
css({ "& > *:not(:last-child)": { borderStyle: "solid", borderBlockEndWidth: "2px", borderBlockEndColor: "var(--ui-border, color-mix(in oklab, CanvasText 16%, transparent))" } })

noScrollbar.name: noScrollbar
noScrollbar.description:
Hides the scrollbar across Chrome/Safari, legacy Edge, and Firefox, while
the element stays scrollable by wheel, touch, keyboard, and script. Pair
with `u.scroll()`/`u.overflow()` on the same element.
noScrollbar.summary: Hides the scrollbar across Chrome/Safari, legacy Edge, and Firefox, while the element stays scrollable by wheel, touch, keyboard, and script.

overflow.name: overflow
overflow.description:
Applies `overflow`, defaulting to `"hidden"`. An axis object sets only the
axes it names and leaves the rest untouched; prefer its `inline`/`block`
keys over `x`/`y` to stay correct under RTL and vertical writing modes.

overflowAnchor.name: overflowAnchor
overflowAnchor.description:
Applies `overflow-anchor`, the browser's choice of which element holds the
scroll position steady as content above it resizes. The `"none"` default
suits infinite-scroll sentinels, whose own growth fights anchoring.
overflowAnchor.summary: Applies `overflow-anchor`, the browser's choice of which element holds the scroll position steady as content above it resizes.

overflowBlock.name: overflowBlock
overflowBlock.description:
Applies `overflow-block`, independently of the inline axis. The block axis
follows writing mode and direction, so the utility stays correct under RTL
and vertical writing modes.
overflowBlock.summary: Applies `overflow-block`, independently of the inline axis.

overflowInline.name: overflowInline
overflowInline.description:
Applies `overflow-inline`, independently of the block axis. The inline axis
follows writing mode and direction, so the utility stays correct under RTL
and vertical writing modes.
overflowInline.summary: Applies `overflow-inline`, independently of the block axis.

overflowX.name: overflowX
overflowX.description: Applies `overflow-x`, independently of the block axis.
overflowX.summary: Applies `overflow-x`, independently of the block axis.

overflowY.name: overflowY
overflowY.description: Applies `overflow-y`, independently of the inline axis.
overflowY.summary: Applies `overflow-y`, independently of the inline axis.

overscrollBehavior.name: overscrollBehavior
overscrollBehavior.description:
Applies `overscroll-behavior`, defaulting to `"contain"`: a scroll past the
end stays inside this element and the platform affordance — iOS
rubber-banding, Android pull-to-refresh — survives. `"none"` suppresses it.
overscrollBehavior.summary: Applies `overscroll-behavior`, defaulting to `"contain"`: a scroll past the end stays inside this element and the platform affordance — iOS rubber-banding, Android pull-to-refresh — survives.

scroll.name: scroll
scroll.description:
Turns the element into a scroll container that reveals a scrollbar only
where content actually overflows the given axis, defaulting to `"both"`.
Composes `u.overflowX("auto")`/`u.overflowY("auto")` for the selected axis.
scroll.summary: Turns the element into a scroll container that reveals a scrollbar only where content actually overflows the given axis, defaulting to `"both"`.

scrollbarColor.name: scrollbarColor
scrollbarColor.description:
Themes a scroll container's scrollbar via the standard `scrollbar-color`
property, supported by Firefox and modern Chromium alike through plain
CSS. Inherits down the tree, theming nested scroll containers too.
scrollbarColor.summary: Themes a scroll container's scrollbar via the standard `scrollbar-color` property, supported by Firefox and modern Chromium alike through plain CSS.

scrollbarGutter.name: scrollbarGutter
scrollbarGutter.description:
Applies `scrollbar-gutter`, defaulting to `"stable"`, so the container is
already the size it settles at and content holds its position the moment a
scrollbar appears. Takes effect on a scroll container (`u.scroll()`).
scrollbarGutter.summary: Applies `scrollbar-gutter`, defaulting to `"stable"`, so the container is already the size it settles at and content holds its position the moment a scrollbar appears.

scrollBehavior.name: scrollBehavior
scrollBehavior.description:
Applies `scroll-behavior`, defaulting to `"smooth"`, so anchor jumps and
programmatic scrolls animate. Smooth scrolling is motion: wrap the call in
`u.motionSafe()` to honor a reduced-motion preference with an instant jump.
scrollBehavior.summary: Applies `scroll-behavior`, defaulting to `"smooth"`, so anchor jumps and programmatic scrolls animate.

scrollMargin.name: scrollMargin
scrollMargin.description:
Applies logical `scroll-margin` on a scroll item, growing the box the
container aligns when it snaps to this item or an anchor jump targets it, so
a sticky header clears only the items that need the extra room.
scrollMargin.summary: Applies logical `scroll-margin` on a scroll item, growing the box the container aligns when it snaps to this item or an anchor jump targets it, so a sticky header clears only the items that need the extra room.

scrollPadding.name: scrollPadding
scrollPadding.description:
Applies logical `scroll-padding` so a scroll snap position or anchor jump
lands clear of a sticky header — set it to the header's height. Follows
`p()`'s 1/2/4-value logical mapping; see [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values).
scrollPadding.summary: Applies logical `scroll-padding` so a scroll snap position or anchor jump lands clear of a sticky header — set it to the header's height.

scrollSnapAlign.name: scrollSnapAlign
scrollSnapAlign.description:
Applies `scroll-snap-align`, defaulting to `"start"`, on the snap *items* —
the children of the scroll container — while `u.scrollSnapType()` goes on the
*container*; swapping the two silently disables snapping either way.
scrollSnapAlign.summary: Applies `scroll-snap-align`, defaulting to `"start"`, on the snap *items* — the children of the scroll container — while `u.scrollSnapType()` goes on the *container*; swapping the two silently disables snapping either way.

scrollSnapStop.name: scrollSnapStop
scrollSnapStop.description:
Applies `scroll-snap-stop` to a snap item, defaulting to `"always"` so a fast
flick rests on the item and one swipe advances exactly one page. `"normal"`
lets momentum carry past it. Pair with `u.scrollSnapAlign()`.
scrollSnapStop.summary: Applies `scroll-snap-stop` to a snap item, defaulting to `"always"` so a fast flick rests on the item and one swipe advances exactly one page.

scrollSnapType.name: scrollSnapType
scrollSnapType.description:
Applies `scroll-snap-type` to a scroll container, defaulting to `"inline
mandatory"`, the paged-carousel case; pass `"none"` to disable snapping.
Snapped children need `u.scrollSnapAlign()`.
scrollSnapType.summary: Applies `scroll-snap-type` to a scroll container, defaulting to `"inline mandatory"`, the paged-carousel case; pass `"none"` to disable snapping.

thinScrollbar.name: thinScrollbar
thinScrollbar.description:
Requests a thin scrollbar that reserves its gutter up front, so layout
stays put whether or not the scrollbar is showing. Pair with
`u.scroll()`/`u.overflow()` on the same scroll container.
thinScrollbar.summary: Requests a thin scrollbar that reserves its gutter up front, so layout stays put whether or not the scrollbar is showing.

balance.name: balance
balance.description:
Balances line lengths across a wrapped block, best suited to short text
such as headings, since browsers cap balancing to a small number of
lines. Use pretty for long-form body copy.
balance.summary: Balances line lengths across a wrapped block, best suited to short text such as headings, since browsers cap balancing to a small number of lines.

font.name: font
font.description:
Applies `font-family` from the named font scale (`sans`, `serif`, `mono`,
or an app-extended name) via `var(--ui-font-{name}, fallback)`.
`"inherit"` and `"unset"` pass through unchanged as literal CSS keywords.
font.summary: Applies `font-family` from the named font scale (`sans`, `serif`, `mono`, or an app-extended name) via `var(--ui-font-{name}, fallback)`.

fontSize.name: fontSize
fontSize.description:
Applies `font-size` from the named text scale (`xs` through `9xl`, or an
app-extended name), resolving the same token as `u.text()`'s font-size
half but touching only `font-size`, leaving line-height fully caller-set.
fontSize.summary: Applies `font-size` from the named text scale (`xs` through `9xl`, or an app-extended name), resolving the same token as `u.text()`'s font-size half but touching only `font-size`, leaving line-height fully caller-set.

fontVariantNumeric.name: fontVariantNumeric
fontVariantNumeric.description:
Sets `font-variant-numeric`; `u.tabularNums()` covers the common
tabular-nums case and shares the same declaration. Each keyword names an
OpenType feature — a font that lacks it renders unchanged digits.
fontVariantNumeric.summary: Sets `font-variant-numeric`; `u.tabularNums()` covers the common tabular-nums case and shares the same declaration.

hyphens.name: hyphens
hyphens.description:
Lets long words break with a hyphen instead of forcing the line short.
`"auto"` hyphenates only when the element or an ancestor carries a `lang`
attribute to pick a dictionary from — omit it and nothing hyphenates.
hyphens.summary: Lets long words break with a hyphen instead of forcing the line short.

leading.name: leading
leading.description:
Applies `line-height`. Named values resolve through
`var(--ui-leading-{name}, fallback)`, so an app can override the scale
without losing the default; numbers and other strings pass through unchanged.

lineClamp.name: lineClamp
lineClamp.description:
Truncates text via the `-webkit-line-clamp` trick. `lines` is
stringified because the CSS serializer appends `px` to unlisted unitless
properties, which would invalidate the declaration and clamp nothing.

nowrap.name: nowrap
nowrap.description:
Prevents text from wrapping onto multiple lines, letting it overflow its
box instead. Pair with truncate when overflow should end in an
ellipsis rather than spill out.
nowrap.summary: Prevents text from wrapping onto multiple lines, letting it overflow its box instead.

overflowWrap.name: overflowWrap
overflowWrap.description:
Applies `overflow-wrap`, breaking a word only when it would otherwise
overflow a bounded inline size, while ordinary text keeps its normal
break points — ideal for a long URL, hash, or identifier in a narrow column.
overflowWrap.summary: Applies `overflow-wrap`, breaking a word only when it would otherwise overflow a bounded inline size, while ordinary text keeps its normal break points — ideal for a long URL, hash, or identifier in a narrow column.

pretty.name: pretty
pretty.description:
Avoids leaving a short orphan word alone on the last line of a wrapped
block, scaling to long-form body copy since browsers don't cap how many
lines it applies to.
pretty.summary: Avoids leaving a short orphan word alone on the last line of a wrapped block, scaling to long-form body copy since browsers don't cap how many lines it applies to.

tabSize.name: tabSize
tabSize.description:
Applies `tab-size`. A bare number is stringified so it stays unitless — CSS
would otherwise read it as a `px` length — while a string such as `"4ch"`
passes through unchanged as a CSS length.

tabularNums.name: tabularNums
tabularNums.description:
Applies `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so digits render at a fixed
width instead of their proportional metrics — a running total, countdown,
or one-time-code field reads without its layout shifting as digits change.
tabularNums.summary: Applies `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so digits render at a fixed width instead of their proportional metrics — a running total, countdown, or one-time-code field reads without its layout shifting as digits change.

text.name: text
text.description:
Applies `font-size` and its paired `line-height` from the named text scale
through matching `var(--ui-text-*)` / `var(--ui-leading-*)` properties, so
an extended name inherits a sensible default leading before defining one.
text.summary: Applies `font-size` and its paired `line-height` from the named text scale through matching `var(--ui-text-*)` / `var(--ui-leading-*)` properties, so an extended name inherits a sensible default leading before defining one.

textAlign.name: textAlign
textAlign.description:
Applies `text-align` using the logical `start`/`end` keywords so alignment
flips automatically under `dir="rtl"`. A raw value such as `"left"` or
`"right"` is also accepted for alignment that must stay physical.
textAlign.summary: Applies `text-align` using the logical `start`/`end` keywords so alignment flips automatically under `dir="rtl"`.

textDecoration.name: textDecoration
textDecoration.description:
Applies `text-decoration-line` from a bare value, or sets only the given
keys from a text-decoration options object. `thickness` and `offset` are
kept separate because `text-decoration`'s shorthand cannot set or reset them.
textDecoration.summary: Applies `text-decoration-line` from a bare value, or sets only the given keys from a text-decoration options object.

tracking.name: tracking
tracking.description:
Applies `letter-spacing` from the named tracking scale, resolving through
`var(--ui-tracking-{name}, fallback)` so the scale works before an app defines
the variable; any other string is treated as a raw `letter-spacing` value.
tracking.summary: Applies `letter-spacing` from the named tracking scale, resolving through `var(--ui-tracking-{name}, fallback)` so the scale works before an app defines the variable; any other string is treated as a raw `letter-spacing` value.

truncate.name: truncate
truncate.summary: Truncates single-line text with an ellipsis once it overflows its box; requires a bounded inline size (`max-inline-size`, a flex/grid item with `min-inline-size: 0`, or similar) or there is nothing to overflow against.

type.name: type
type.description:
Combines text's `font-size`/`line-height` pair with the base sans
font family, always opinionating the style to `sans`. Pair `u.text()` with
an explicit `u.font()` when another family is needed.
type.summary: Combines text's `font-size`/`line-height` pair with the base sans font family, always opinionating the style to `sans`.

examples.output: css({ fontFamily: "var(--ui-font-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif)", fontSize: "var(--ui-text-lg, 1.125rem)", lineHeight: "var(--ui-leading-lg, 1.5)" })

verticalAlign.name: verticalAlign
verticalAlign.description:
Applies `vertical-align`, e.g. for aligning an inline-block icon against
adjacent text.

weight.name: weight
weight.description:
Applies `font-weight`. Named values alias the standard numeric weight
scale (`thin` 100 through `black` 900); a raw number passes through
unchanged for values the named scale doesn't cover.

whiteSpace.name: whiteSpace
whiteSpace.description:
Applies `white-space`; also written by `u.nowrap()`, `u.truncate()`, and
`u.visuallyHidden()`, so pick one. Defaults to `pre-wrap`, keeping
preformatted line breaks while still wrapping in a narrow container.
whiteSpace.summary: Applies `white-space`; also written by `u.nowrap()`, `u.truncate()`, and `u.visuallyHidden()`, so pick one.

debug.name: debug
debug.description:
Outlines the host in red during development and resolves to an empty style
tree elsewhere, so the call is safe to leave in committed code. `"nested"`
extends the outline to every descendant to inspect a full box model.
debug.summary: Outlines the host in red during development and resolves to an empty style tree elsewhere, so the call is safe to leave in committed code.

forcedColorAdjust.name: forcedColorAdjust
forcedColorAdjust.description:
Applies `forced-color-adjust`, defaulting to `"none"` so author colours
survive where colour itself carries the information — swatches, chart
legends, syntax highlighting. Scope it with `u.forcedColors()`.
forcedColorAdjust.summary: Applies `forced-color-adjust`, defaulting to `"none"` so author colours survive where colour itself carries the information — swatches, chart legends, syntax highlighting.

visuallyHidden.name: visuallyHidden
visuallyHidden.description:
Clips the host to a `1px` box taken out of layout flow, keeping its native
focusability and tab order intact so screen readers and keyboard users
still reach it.
visuallyHidden.summary: Clips the host to a `1px` box taken out of layout flow, keeping its native focusability and tab order intact so screen readers and keyboard users still reach it.

examples.output:
css({
  position: "absolute",
  inlineSize: "1px",
  blockSize: "1px",
  padding: "0",
  margin: "-1px",
  overflow: "hidden",
  clip: "rect(0, 0, 0, 0)",
  whiteSpace: "nowrap",
  borderWidth: "0",
})

aspect.name: aspect
aspect.description:
Applies `aspect-ratio`, either from a width/height pair or one of the named
ratios in `AspectRatioName`. Ratios vary too continuously for a full token
family to pay for itself, so only a handful of common shapes get names.
aspect.summary: Applies `aspect-ratio`, either from a width/height pair or one of the named ratios in `AspectRatioName`.

bleed.name: bleed
bleed.description:
Pulls the host past its container's inline padding by `value` on both
sides via a negative inline margin — for a full-bleed image or divider
inside an otherwise padded section, composing `u.mi()` with a negated length.
bleed.summary: Pulls the host past its container's inline padding by `value` on both sides via a negative inline margin — for a full-bleed image or divider inside an otherwise padded section, composing `u.mi()` with a negated length.

bs.name: bs
bs.description:
Applies `block-size` — the logical height, which is the physical width in
a vertical writing mode.
bs.summary: Applies `block-size` — the logical height, which is the physical width in a vertical writing mode.

circle.name: circle
circle.description:
A shape pattern for circular boxes: a square aspect ratio plus full
radius — an avatar frame, a status dot, an icon badge. Composes
`u.aspect("square")` and `u.rounded("full")`.
circle.summary: A shape pattern for circular boxes: a square aspect ratio plus full radius — an avatar frame, a status dot, an icon badge.

corner.name: corner
corner.description:
The primitive `corner-shape` utility. Composes `u.supports()` so the
declaration only applies behind `@supports`, leaving unsupported
browsers with their normal `border-radius` shape.

fit.name: fit
fit.description:
Applies `object-fit`, shaping how a container-sized media element
(`img`, `video`) fills its box.
fit.summary: Applies `object-fit`, shaping how a container-sized media element (`img`, `video`) fills its box.

height.name: height
height.description:
Applies the physical `height` property, keeping element size tied to
the viewport axis across writing-modes and directions. Prefer `u.bs()`
(`block-size`) for content that should track the logical block axis.
height.summary: Applies the physical `height` property, keeping element size tied to the viewport axis across writing-modes and directions.

is.name: is
is.description:
Applies `inline-size` — the logical width, which is the physical height
in a vertical writing mode.
is.summary: Applies `inline-size` — the logical width, which is the physical height in a vertical writing mode.

m.name: m
m.description:
Applies logical margin using the spacing scale, `"auto"`, or a raw CSS
length. Follows the same 1/2/4-value logical mapping as `p()` — see
[MDN: logical properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values).
m.summary: Applies logical margin using the spacing scale, `"auto"`, or a raw CSS length.

marginLeft.name: marginLeft
marginLeft.description:
Sets the physical `margin-left` property directly, pinned to the fixed
left edge regardless of writing direction. Prefer `u.mi()`
(`margin-inline`) for direction-aware margins.
marginLeft.summary: Sets the physical `margin-left` property directly, pinned to the fixed left edge regardless of writing direction.

marginRight.name: marginRight
marginRight.description:
Sets the physical `margin-right` property directly, pinned to the fixed
right edge regardless of writing direction. Prefer `u.mi()`
(`margin-inline`) for direction-aware margins.
marginRight.summary: Sets the physical `margin-right` property directly, pinned to the fixed right edge regardless of writing direction.

maxHeight.name: maxHeight
maxHeight.description:
Applies the physical `max-height` property, for components whose sizing
tracks the physical viewport axis. Use `u.maxBs()` (`max-block-size`) for
the logical block-axis default.
maxHeight.summary: Applies the physical `max-height` property, for components whose sizing tracks the physical viewport axis.

maxWidth.name: maxWidth
maxWidth.description:
Applies the physical `max-width` property, for elements whose sizing is
genuinely tied to the physical viewport axis. Prefer `u.maxIs()`
(`max-inline-size`) for the logical default.
maxWidth.summary: Applies the physical `max-width` property, for elements whose sizing is genuinely tied to the physical viewport axis.

mb.name: mb
mb.description:
Applies `margin-block`. One value applies both block edges; two values
map to block-start then block-end.

mbe.name: mbe
mbe.description:
Applies `margin-block-end` — the trailing block edge, the bottom edge in
a horizontal writing mode.
mbe.summary: Applies `margin-block-end` — the trailing block edge, the bottom edge in a horizontal writing mode.

mbs.name: mbs
mbs.description:
Applies `margin-block-start` — the leading block edge, the top edge in a
horizontal writing mode.
mbs.summary: Applies `margin-block-start` — the leading block edge, the top edge in a horizontal writing mode.

mi.name: mi
mi.description:
Applies `margin-inline`. One value applies both inline edges; two values
map to inline-start then inline-end.

mie.name: mie
mie.description:
Applies `margin-inline-end` — the trailing inline edge, which is the
right edge in `ltr` and the left edge in `rtl`.
mie.summary: Applies `margin-inline-end` — the trailing inline edge, which is the right edge in `ltr` and the left edge in `rtl`.

minHeight.name: minHeight
minHeight.description:
Applies the physical `min-height` property. Prefer `u.minBs()`
(`min-block-size`) unless the element's sizing must track the physical
viewport axis regardless of writing-mode or direction.

minWidth.name: minWidth
minWidth.description:
Applies the physical `min-width` property, for elements whose sizing is
tied to the physical viewport axis. Prefer `u.minIs()`
(`min-inline-size`) for the logical default.
minWidth.summary: Applies the physical `min-width` property, for elements whose sizing is tied to the physical viewport axis.

mis.name: mis
mis.description:
Applies `margin-inline-start` — the leading inline edge, which is the
left edge in `ltr` and the right edge in `rtl`.
mis.summary: Applies `margin-inline-start` — the leading inline edge, which is the left edge in `ltr` and the right edge in `rtl`.

objectPosition.name: objectPosition
objectPosition.description:
Applies `object-position`, choosing which part of a replaced element's
cropped content stays visible, keeping a subject's face in frame once
`u.fit("cover")` crops it. Only works with `u.fit()` on replaced elements.
objectPosition.summary: Applies `object-position`, choosing which part of a replaced element's cropped content stays visible, keeping a subject's face in frame once `u.fit("cover")` crops it.

p.name: p
p.description:
Applies logical padding using the spacing scale or a raw CSS length. One
value applies all sides; two values map to block then inline; four values
map to block-start, inline-end, block-end, and inline-start.
p.summary: Applies logical padding using the spacing scale or a raw CSS length.

paddingLeft.name: paddingLeft
paddingLeft.description:
Applies the physical `padding-left` property, for padding pinned to a
fixed, physical viewport edge — such as a safe-area-inset offset on a
docked panel. Prefer `u.pis()`/`u.pi()` for logical inline padding.
paddingLeft.summary: Applies the physical `padding-left` property, for padding pinned to a fixed, physical viewport edge — such as a safe-area-inset offset on a docked panel.

paddingRight.name: paddingRight
paddingRight.description:
Applies the physical `padding-right` property, for padding pinned to a
fixed, physical viewport edge — such as a safe-area-inset offset on a
docked panel. Prefer `u.pie()`/`u.pi()` for logical inline padding.
paddingRight.summary: Applies the physical `padding-right` property, for padding pinned to a fixed, physical viewport edge — such as a safe-area-inset offset on a docked panel.

pb.name: pb
pb.description:
Applies `padding-block`. One value applies both block edges; two values
map to block-start then block-end.

pbe.name: pbe
pbe.description:
Applies `padding-block-end` — the trailing block edge, the bottom edge in
a horizontal writing mode.
pbe.summary: Applies `padding-block-end` — the trailing block edge, the bottom edge in a horizontal writing mode.

pbs.name: pbs
pbs.description:
Applies `padding-block-start` — the leading block edge, the top edge in
a horizontal writing mode.
pbs.summary: Applies `padding-block-start` — the leading block edge, the top edge in a horizontal writing mode.

pi.name: pi
pi.description:
Applies `padding-inline`. One value applies both inline edges; two values
map to inline-start then inline-end.

pie.name: pie
pie.description:
Applies `padding-inline-end` — the trailing inline edge, which is the
right edge in `ltr` and the left edge in `rtl`.
pie.summary: Applies `padding-inline-end` — the trailing inline edge, which is the right edge in `ltr` and the left edge in `rtl`.

pis.name: pis
pis.description:
Applies `padding-inline-start` — the leading inline edge, which is the
left edge in `ltr` and the right edge in `rtl`.
pis.summary: Applies `padding-inline-start` — the leading inline edge, which is the left edge in `ltr` and the right edge in `rtl`.

safeAreaPadding.name: safeAreaPadding
safeAreaPadding.description:
Pads the given physical `side` by its `env(safe-area-inset-{side})` value,
falling back to `fallback` (`"0px"` by default) on platforms with no safe
area to avoid. Sets only that one physical padding property.
safeAreaPadding.summary: Pads the given physical `side` by its `env(safe-area-inset-{side})` value, falling back to `fallback` (`"0px"` by default) on platforms with no safe area to avoid.

squircle.name: squircle
squircle.description:
A shape pattern for continuous rounded corners: sets a radius, then
refines it with `corner-shape` where supported, so every browser renders
at least the plain rounded shape. Composes `u.rounded()` and `u.corner()`.
